nomenclature.etymology_html:
-Gymnosporia : From the Greek gymnos "naked" and sporo "seed", with naked-seed.
-Emarginata : Notched at the apex, in reference to the leaves of the plant.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Gymnosporia emarginata is smooth and light brown-coloured. Gymnosporia emarginata has sharp thorns , growing axillary from the branches or apically at the end of the branchlets.
stem_bark.text_html:
The bark of Gymnosporia emarginata is smooth and light brown-coloured.
Gymnosporia emarginata has sharp thorns, growing axillary from the branches or apically at the end of the branchlets.

seed.text: The seeds of Gymnosporia emarginata are ovoid and 3-4 mm across with a fleshy aril. There are 2 seeds in each valve of the capsule.

fruit.text: The fruit of Gymnosporia emarginata is a subglobose and trilocular capsule. The fruit is 6-8 mm across, dehiscing into 3 valves.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Gymnosporia emarginata is a subglobose and trilocular capsule. The fruit is 6-8 mm across, dehiscing into 3 valves.

flower.text: The flowers of Gymnosporia emarginata are grouped in short axillary or terminal cymes. The peduncle is reduced. The flowers are 5-merous. The calyx is composed of a 5 mm long tube and 5 mm long lobes. The calyx is light green yellowish-coloured and glabrous. The corolla is composed of 5 white-coloured and glabrous petals. The petals are ovate and 3-4 mm long and 2-3 mm wide. The androecium is composed of 5 stamens with 2-3 mm long filaments and small and ovoid anthers. The style is short with 3 stigmas. The ovary is 3-celled with 2 ovules per cell. The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Gymnosporia emarginata grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous and glabrous on both sides. The leaves have a 5 mm long petiole . The leaf of Gymnosporia emarginata is 3-5 cm long and 2.5-3.5 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate, obovate or spathulate, the apex is obtuse or acute and often emarginate, the base is rounded or cuneate and the margins are entire (somtimes obscurely crenate). The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Gymnosporia emarginata is a thorny and deciduous shrub , growing up to 5-6 m high.
habit.text_html: Gymnosporia emarginata is a thorny and deciduous shrub, growing up to 5-6 m high.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Gymnosporia emarginata is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Gymnosporia emarginata is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation. The ripe and dry capsules of Gymnosporia emarginata opens to scatter the seeds.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Gymnosporia emarginata is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Gymnosporia emarginata is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
    The ripe and dry capsules of Gymnosporia emarginata opens to scatter the seeds.

reforestation.text: Gymnosporia emarginata is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. It thrives in open areas (it prefers full sunlight). The species is propagated by seeds. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Gymnosporia emarginata is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. It thrives in open areas (it prefers full sunlight).
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
